prediction.likelyOutcome: The Developers have a genuinely strong liability argument on the enforced-delay/premature-default issue and the City's immunity waiver removes its best threshold defense, but the single biggest damages category (garage lost-profits, ~$11M) is legally fragile as speculative new-business profits, and even the more defensible reliance-damages categories for the Tower and Theater (~$8.6M combined) face a serious causation fight over whether the Developers' own financing collapse — not the City's default notices — actually killed the project. Net expected recovery is meaningfully below both the full ~$20.9M in stated trial subtotals and the baseline model's $14-24M band, landing in the mid-single to high-single digit millions once causation risk and the speculativeness of the lost-profits theory are properly discounted, with the City's counterclaim unlikely to produce a significant offsetting recovery.

outcome.description: After an October 2022 bench trial the district court found the City breached the Development Agreement (and tortiously interfered with the construction loan) and awarded Parking LLC $4,353,677 in expectancy damages (garage development fee, savings under the stipulated price, and interest) against the City, rejecting all other claimed damages and the City's counterclaims; court costs were taxed to the City. The Iowa Supreme Court affirmed the breach-of-contract judgment and the $4,353,677 award on June 12, 2026, vacated the tortious-interference judgment, and affirmed the denial of the Developers' additional damages.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; tortious-interference liability vacated without changing the amount.
